title: How to Spur People On to Success
coreMove: Praise the smallest real improvement out loud and by name, before the person decides whether to keep trying

exampleSpecs.domain: a piano teacher working with a nine-year-old who botched the left hand of a Clementi sonatina but landed two measures cleanly
exampleSpecs.audience: a private music teacher dreading the parent's question about progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the child quits lessons by spring or stays with the instrument long enough to love it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the teacher pauses on the two clean measures, names them specifically by bar number, and watches the child's posture change before saying anything about the rest

exampleSpecs.domain: a line cook on his third week being told his knife cuts are still uneven, except for the brunoise he turned out at family meal
exampleSpecs.audience: a sous chef who was trained by yelling and is trying not to repeat it
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the cook quits before his fourth shift or stays and becomes the station's most reliable prep
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the sous chef opens with the brunoise by name, in the kitchen where other cooks can hear, before mentioning anything about the chiffonade

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospice nurse coaching a new aide who froze the first two times a patient's family cried, then sat through it the third time without leaving the room
exampleSpecs.audience: a charge nurse responsible for retaining aides in a job most people quit within ninety days
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a naturally gentle person believes she belongs in this work or transfers to billing by Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the charge nurse names the third visit specifically and tells the aide what she did right, with no qualifier and no but-clause attached

exampleSpecs.domain: a father reading his teenage son's college application essay, the fourth draft, which is still uneven but has one paragraph about his grandfather that lands
exampleSpecs.audience: a father who tends to fix things sentence by sentence and has watched his son stop showing him drafts
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the son ever asks for his father's help on the next essay or goes silent through senior year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the father reads the grandfather paragraph aloud back to his son and says exactly what worked in it before turning a page

exampleSpecs.domain: a regional sales manager reviewing a struggling rep's call recordings and finding one call where the rep finally stopped pitching and asked a question
exampleSpecs.audience: a regional sales manager about to put the rep on a performance plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the rep walks into next week believing he can sell or rehearses his resignation in the parking lot
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager plays the one good question back to the rep and tells him that is the move, not the close, and watches the rep write it down

exampleSpecs.domain: a swim coach working with a forty-year-old beginner who has been afraid of the deep end for thirty years and yesterday let go of the wall for two seconds
exampleSpecs.audience: a recreation-center swim coach with eight adults in the lane
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the woman comes back next Tuesday or quietly cancels the rest of her sessions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coach singles out the two seconds at the end of class, in front of the other adults, and says she saw it and what it meant
